text: The city council voted on Tuesday to extend the downtown bike lane network by twelve kilometers over the next two years. The plan, which costs about 4 million dollars, connects the university campus to the central train station. Supporters said the lanes would cut car traffic during rush hour, while several shop owners worried about losing parking spaces in front of their stores. Construction starts in March, beginning with the section near the station. The council also asked the transport office to publish monthly reports on cyclist numbers so the effect can be measured.
